discovery: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene: prediction and discovery of flat-band correlated insulators and superconductivity in moire materials

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional materials and correlated electrons
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that twisting two graphene layers to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands nearly flat, so that interactions dominate kinetic energy. Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers (Nature 2018) realised this with a tear-and-stack technique for controlling twist angle, and found gate-tunable correlated insulating states and superconductivity in a single device of pure carbon. The work turned twist angle into a new control knob for quantum matter. It founded the field of moire materials, which has since produced orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, Chern insulators and, in twisted semiconductors, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states without a magnetic field. It is a model of a clean theoretical prediction confirmed by an ingenious device experiment, and it has opened a broad experimental platform for strongly correlated and topological physics.
